---
title: "One feature"
subtitle: "A ring of radial gaussians — one feature per A-scan, on the real acquisition calibration"
---

The first realistic geometry: a synthetic choroid whose features sit on its edge,
so that each A-scan crosses **a single gaussian**. Everything the measurement
chain sees comes from that one feature moving sub-pixel — which is the cleanest
case, and therefore the upper bound on what the chain can do.

## The concept : a ring that breathes

![](figures_simulation/concept_anneau.png){width=92%}

![](figures_simulation/concept_kymographe.png){width=86%}

A ring of radial gaussians ($R_0 = 500\ \mu m$, $\sigma$ drawn between 10 and
20 µm, angles drawn once and frozen for the whole sweep) inflating and deflating
radially on a 1.0 → 1.3 Hz chirp, rendered on the **real acquisition
calibration** : 11.4 µm/px lateral, 3.9 µm/px axial, 17.9 Hz, 401 frames
(22.4 s) — read from an actual Spectralis XML export, not invented.

- pixels are **not square** : a ring that is circular in µm is an ellipse in the
  pixel grid — and the pixel grid is what the SVD works on
- the typical 6 µm peak-to-peak amplitude is **1.54 px axially** : the motion is
  **sub-pixel**, invisible frame by frame, and only shows up as an intensity
  modulation once the temporal mean is removed

## Measurement chain

Frames are injected into a minimal fake `registered_video` and go through the
package's own chain, exactly as in `Astronauts/compute_one_cycle_pixel_svd.py` :

`PixelTraceSource` → `DecomposedTraceSource(method="svd")` →
`LombScargleRateEstimator` → `OptimizedSpectralCombination` →
`HilbertPhaseEstimator`, driven by `PulseExtractor`.

No video cube is saved: each run is fully determined by its parameters + seed, so
it is regenerable on demand. Saved per run (`.npz`) : $U$, $V$, $S$, rate/phase
diagnostics, and the ground truth (imposed radial displacement, instantaneous
chirp frequency), plus one summary line in `summary.csv`.

## Results : one factor at a time

![](figures_simulation/resultats_phaseA.png){width=90%}

554 runs. *Detected* = `LombScargle` confidence high/medium **and** relative
frequency error $\leq 10\%$. Each panel varies one factor, the others held at the
value printed above it.

- **amplitude** : 100 % from 0.5 to 10 µm — but at zero noise *and* zero jitter,
  so this panel bounds nothing on its own
- **image noise** : 100 % up to $\times 5$ the realistic level, 70 % at $\times 8$ ;
  correlation with ground truth $1.00 \rightarrow 0.83$
- **jitter $x$ and $y$** : 100 % detection up to 4 px of either, at the typical
  6 µm amplitude ; correlation degrades gently to $\simeq 0.89$

Taken **one at a time**, none of these factors defeats the chain at a realistic
amplitude — the correlation erodes well before the detection does.

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
## Read this together with the combined grid

"One at a time" is exactly the weakness of this page. Crossing the factors
changes the conclusion: at 1 µm amplitude, several jitter combinations drop to
**0 % detection** even though no single factor did anything on its own. See
[Mixtures](sim-mixtures.qmd).
:::
